title: Probe Keeper — microbench tracker (personal)
content:
One-page scratch sheet for ad-hoc microbench runs. Purpose: quick capture of per-run latency/throughput and short notes so I can iterate experiments without a full bench dashboard. Keep it light, chronological.

Run metadata columns (CSV-style below):
date,run_id,model,precision,batch_size,seq_len,avg_latency_ms,p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_tps,total_tokens,notes
2025-10-12,run-001,t5-small,int8,4,64,23.4,21.0,39.6,44.3,11200,initial quantized run; weird p95 spike on warmup
2025-10-13,run-002,t5-small,int8+kv,8,64,17.1,16.2,24.8,90.7,23040,enabled local KV cache prefixing => throughput up x2.05
2025-10-15,run-003,open-llama-7b,fp16,2,128,86.2,82.0,140.5,9.2,5120,baseline fp16, small batch to keep latency low
2025-10-20,run-004,open-llama-7b,int4,4,128,48.7,45.2,72.1,17.8,10240,int4 quant w/ custom kernel, quality check pending
2025-10-28,run-005,open-llama-7b,int4,8,64,29.6,28.0,48.0,35.0,17920,burst mode; noticed memory pressure at node-level
2025-10-30,run-006,redwood-verified-3b,fp16,16,32,12.9,11.8,20.2,240.5,15360,high batch for embeddings-like throughput test

Quick observations:
- KV cache gave the biggest cost/latency win for short sequential prompts (run-002). Need to quantify token hit-rate distribution.
- int4 looks promising for 7b but p95 still has tail events tied to GC spikes on host (check SRE logs).
- Large batch sizes reduce per-token cost but add to end-to-end tail latency; tradeoff depends on SLO.

Mini action list (ad-hoc):
- (A) Re-run run-004 with kernel tweak from PR #834 and capture system-level metrics (nvml + iostat) — assigned to me, target 2025-11-05.
- (B) Add a small prefix set to measure KV hit rate: 1000 requests with repeat prefix patterns, capture hit% and avg latency — ask Lucas for tooling snippet.
- (C) Evaluate quality: run 200 prompt pairs (fp16 vs int4) and compute embedding/cosine drift + avg token perplexity.

Notes to self (short snippets):
- When logging to a full bench dashboard, include 'run_tag' and 'kernel_hash' fields to make results reproducible.
- Use per-request tracing to isolate whether p95 is model compute or host I/O.
- If p95 correlates with host memory spike, try cgroups swap limits and scheduler tweak.

Lightweight checklist before marking a run for sharing: (check when done)
- [ ] reproduce run twice at different times of day
- [ ] collect nvml/gpu-util / dmesg / host-cpu during run
- [ ] attach config.yaml for that run (model, quant, kernels, request pattern)
- [ ] short summary sentence for Slack thread

Scratch formulas (manual):
- throughput_tps = total_tokens / (avg_latency_ms / 1000)  # rough, tokens per second
- cost_est = gpu_hourly * (total_tokens / tokens_per_hour_est)  # back-of-envelope

Freeform ramble (notes-to-self):
"KV caching seems undervalued in our default suggestions. For short convo workloads, caching > quant in terms of latency win. Need a small writeup comparing: single-token latency vs throughput vs token cost across sweeps. Also compare fallback behaviour: when cache miss, measure extra 1.5x latency on average. Could be a strong default for hosted small requests tier."

End of sheet.
summary: Personal microbench ledger capturing quick runs across t5, open-llama, and redwood-verified models. Focused on quantization, KV caching, batch tradeoffs, and quick next steps.
next_steps: Re-run int4 with kernel tweak (2025-11-05), KV hit-rate batch test, quality sweep fp16 vs int4. Prepare short Slack summary once NVML traces attached.
